rules.title: Tenant Protection Act just cause requirement for terminating tenancies
rules.requirement: Once a tenant has lawfully lived in a residential unit for 12 months (or 24 months for at least one tenant if adult tenants were added), the owner may end the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause listed in the statute, and must state that cause in the written notice. For a no-fault termination, the owner must pay relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent, equal to one month's rent. A curable violation must first get a notice with a chance to fix it.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 12 months' occupancy; no-fault relocation assistance = 1 month's rent
rules.quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.

effective_dates.quoted_span: (m) This section shall become operative on April 1, 2024.

sunset_date.quoted_span: (n) This section shall remain in effect only until January 1, 2030, and as of that date is repealed.

exemption_conditions.condition: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy; housing in nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, adult residential facilities; dormitories owned and operated by higher education institutions or K-12 schools
value: residential care facility for the elderly

exemption_conditions.condition: Tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with an owner who maintains their principal residence at the property
Single-family owner-occupied residence where the owner-occupant rents no more than two units or bedrooms (including ADU/JADU), or a mobilehome
Duplex (two units in a single structure) where the owner occupied one unit as principal residence at the start of the tenancy and continues to do so, and neither unit is an ADU/JADU
Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless it is a mobilehome

Separately alienable property (e.g., single-family home or condo) not owned by a REIT, a corporation, an LLC with at least one corporate member, or mobilehome park management, where tenants received the required written exemption notice
Deed-restricted or regulatory-restricted affordable housing for very low, low, or moderate income households, or housing under an affordable housing subsidy agreement
Property subject to a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or a more protective one adopted or amended after that date
exemption_conditions.value: subject to qualifying local just cause ordinance

exemption_conditions.condition: Homeowner of a mobilehome as defined in Section 798.9

coverage.notes: Applies after all tenants have occupied for 12 months, or at least one tenant for 24 months if adult tenants were added before an existing tenant reached 24 months. Housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years is exempt unless it is a mobilehome. Some mobilehome dates differ (e.g., January 1, 2022 / July 1, 2022).

rules.coverage_text: Residential real property, including mobilehome park units, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied the unit for 12 months (or after one tenant reaches 24 months if adult tenants were added). Housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years is excluded unless it is a mobilehome.
rules.exemptions: Transient/tourist hotels; nonprofit hospitals, religious, extended care, elderly residential care, and adult residential facilities; school or university dormitories; units where the tenant shares a bathroom or kitchen with a resident owner; single-family owner-occupied homes renting no more than two units or bedrooms, and mobilehomes in that context; owner-occupied duplexes with no ADU/JADU; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within 15 years (except mobilehomes); separately alienable units not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, if the statutory exemption notice was given; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; property covered by qualifying local just cause ordinances; homeowners of mobilehomes.
rules.interaction: Yields to local just cause ordinances adopted on or before September 1, 2019, and to ones adopted or amended after that date that are more protective. A property cannot be subject to both. Local ordinances adopted after September 1, 2019 that are less protective cannot be enforced unless this section is repealed. Relocation assistance is credited against relocation assistance required by other laws.

tool_input.notes: The text gives two dates: the section says it 'shall become operative on April 1, 2024', and the history note says the AB 1529 amendment is 'Effective January 1, 2026'. Both are recorded. No signing date is given.
